transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-09
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 48 minutes (recording truncated at ~48:30)
Attendees: Maya Bennett (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO, Helios), Luis Ortega (Lead ML Eng, Helios), Samir Patel (Infra Lead, Helios)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on POC success criteria (latency / cost / throughput), reserved GPU sizing with burst capacity, fallback policy requirements for graceful degradation, and next steps to run benchmarks. Agreed to a hybrid reserved+burst pilot with a planned synthetic benchmark run next week and a follow-up deeper technical run with logs.

Topics Covered:
- Objectives & success criteria (p50/p95 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens)
- Workload profile (seq lengths, QPS patterns, batching potential)
- Reserved GPU sizing + burst budgeting and autoscale windows
- Fallback policies (model variants, queueing, degraded feature modes)
- Benchmarks (microbenchmarks, end-to-end e2e with real requests)
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro — i'm maya, AE on the account, jordan will handle the technical mapping. we got about 45 minutes. sound good?
[00:12] Priya (Helios CTO): yes thanks, quick heads up, we have a 2-part objective: get a POC that proves cost and latency on our real traffic and validate fallback behavior for our critical endpoint.
[00:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): awesome. can you sketch the endpoint? typical sequence length, token mix, avg request size?
[00:31] Luis (Helios): most requests are short — 20 to 80 tokens — but we have a 5% tail that goes to 400-1k tokens for long-form summarization. QPS is bursty: baseline 40 qps with spikes to ~600 during report drops, those spikes last 3–7 minutes.
[00:48] Samir (Helios): infra constraints: must run in our VPC, keys managed via our KMS, SOC2 a must. also prefer reserved capacity to hit predictable billing for the pilot.
[01:04] Maya: good notes. our typical approach is hybrid: reserved capacity sized for baseline + some headroom, with burst pool for short spikes and fallbacks to smaller quantized variants if burst saturates. does that align with your constraints?
[01:20] Priya: yes, particularly the fallback behavior is critical — we can't have 20s responses during a spike. acceptable tradeoff is lower quality summarization if latency stays under 2s p95 for short requests, and 6s for long-form tails — is that feasible?
[01:36] Jordan: depends on model choices. if you use a 7B quantized variant for progressive fallback we can hit sub-2s p95 for 20–80 tokens on A100-like hardware. for the long tail you'll need reserved capacity or queued processing unless you're okay with a slightly longer p95.
[01:52] Luis: what's your recommended reserved GPU count for baseline 40 qps with 5% long tail? we want to avoid overcommit.
[02:00] Jordan: quick calc: assuming 7B model, steady-state throughput per GPU is ~250–350 rps for short sequences with batching. for conservative sizing, reserve 1 GPU for every 200 steady qps baseline. for 40 qps baseline, 1 reserved GPU is plenty with autoscale min at 1. then add a burst pool sized to handle 600 qps spikes — that would be roughly 2–3 extra GPUs depending on burst duration and batching behavior.
[02:26] Maya: note that burst pool isn't billed at the same rate as reserved; there's a burst pricing window. we'll send an estimated cost comparison.
[02:33] Priya: can you explain the burst fallback sequence? what happens when burst pool is exhausted?
[02:39] Jordan: policy layering: 1) if reserved + burst capacity available, route to full model, 2) if not, route to quantized variant (smaller model) maintained on reserved nodes, 3) if still saturated, queue with short timeout (500–1500ms) and return degraded response (light summarization) or an explanation to the user, 4) as a final safety net, route to cached responses for common prompts.
[03:05] Samir: cache is fine but we need TTL and cache invalidation guidance; also want to know KV cache warmup behavior for chat-like sessions.
[03:14] Jordan: our KV and prefix cache are warm on long-running sessions; during scale-out there’s cold-start latency for large KV caches. recommended: keep session-affine requests on reserved pods and enable prefix caching for the most common workflows. we'll include recommended cache TTLs in the runbook.
[03:32] Priya: timelines — we want results in 2 weeks. meaningful?
[03:36] Maya: yes for an initial synthetic benchmark and quick e2e — two weeks to a baseline report is reasonable if you share traces this week. full production-like run with live traffic needs more time for security approvals.
[03:48] Luis: security: we'll need SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. is Redwood Private required for that?
[03:54] Jordan: not necessarily — the hosted Dedicated option supports KMS integration and audit logs if you choose dedicated pools inside a customer VPC. we can do Private only if you require on-prem air-gapped, but for the pilot Dedicated + VPC peering is common.
[04:12] Maya: can you give a sample success criteria list to sign off?
[04:16] Priya: yes — p95 <= 2s for short requests (20–80 tokens), p95 <= 6s for long requests (400–1000 tokens), sustained baseline cost < $X per 1k tokens (we'll provide targets), zero failed requests during normal baseline, graceful degradation under spikes with clear user messaging.
[04:35] Jordan: we'll codify those in the POC rubric. for benchmarks, we recommend two tracks: 1) microbench (single-model throughput, cold/warm KV cache) and 2) e2e (synthetic traffic based on your traces + small window live traffic).
[04:51] Samir: about quantized variants — are you running INT8 / FP16? we need to be precise for accuracy regressions.
[04:58] Jordan: we support int8 and fp16 variants. for critical LLM outputs we suggest running a quality eval against a set of golden prompts to detect regression beyond an acceptable delta. Redwood Optimize can run a quick A/B on a small holdback set during the POC.
[05:16] Luis: can we run an A/B where 10% of traffic uses full model, 90% uses quantized variant to test quality vs cost?
[05:22] Maya: yes, that's a common pattern. we can do traffic split in the rollout policy and collect token-level cost and latency.
[05:30] Priya: ok brilliant, what's the expected cold-start during an autoscale event? this is a big concern.
[05:36] Jordan: depends on model size and whether you have prewarmed images. typical cold-start for a 7B is ~6–12s without warm cache, for larger models 20–40s. we mitigate with prewarmed pool and staged scale-out, plus queueing with short timeouts. we'll show a plan to keep p95 acceptable.
[05:56] Samir: does Redwood support container image preloading inside our VPC? we want to minimize egress time and image pulls.
[06:02] Jordan: yes, we can provide AMIs or container images pushed to your private registry as part of Dedicated/Private setup. we'll document required permissions.
[06:12] Priya: who owns the rollout policy during POC — us or Redwood?
[06:16] Maya: for the pilot we typically operate in collaborative mode: we propose a default rollout and your infra owner (samir) has final toggles. we'll hand over IaC snippets for your team to take over.
[06:28] Luis: what's a realistic total GPU-hour cost for the two-week pilot baseline tests including burst allowance?
[06:34] Maya: estimate: reserved base (1 x V100/A100 equivalent) + 3 burst GPUs for short spikes results in ~X GPU-hours; we'll provide a line-item estimate in the spreadsheet. this will vary by region and instance type; we'll send scenarios (low/med/high) tomorrow.
[06:54] Priya: benchmarks — please include endpoints for token-level logging so we can validate cost breakdowns.
[07:00] Jordan: yes we'll emit token-level metrics and traces; Redwood Console gives token cost by route and per-model breakdown.
[07:08] Maya: quick clarification on fallback UX — will the application know it's degraded or will we return a normal-looking but lower-quality result?
[07:16] Jordan: you can choose: either a structured response with {"degraded": true, "reason": "quantized fallback"} or a plain response. for POC we recommend structured flags so QA can filter.
[07:29] Samir: our compliance team wants to see audit logs and who triggered fallbacks. can Redwood supply that?
[07:35] Jordan: yes. Dedicated mode with VPC gives audit logs, RBAC traces, and event hooks. we'll include sample log output.
[07:44] Priya: let's talk about timeline concretely — we need a benchmark report by 2027-11-22.
[07:49] Maya: that's two weeks — doable for the synthetic + e2e run if you provide traces this week. we'll plan the benchmark for 2027-11-16 and sync on the run configuration prior.
[07:59] Luis: run config: batch size limits, concurrency targets, sequence length distribution — can you share a template?
[08:05] Jordan: yes, we'll send a benchmark template and a sample k6/locust config. include your 95th percentile traffic window so we hit realistic load.
[08:14] Priya: one more on SLA — for the pilot we need 99.5% availability. is that typical?
[08:19] Maya: dedicated reserved nodes can get close; production SLA needs enterprise contract but for pilot we'll aim for stable reserved capacity and monitor.
[08:26] Samir: if the burst pool is exhausted and we hit quantized fallback, do you queue or do you shed traffic?
[08:32] Jordan: we support both. default is short queue with graceful degradation; you can choose shedding if timeouts are strict. we can configure circuit breaker thresholds — e.g., queue up to 1k requests or 1s delay then fallback.
[08:45] Maya: want to call out success gates for POC sign-off: 1) benchmark metrics hit p95 targets, 2) cost per 1k tokens within agreed band, 3) quality regression < 5% on golden prompt set, 4) security checklist met (KMS, SSO), 5) handover plan.
[09:05] Priya: agreed. we'll internal sign-off 3 days after benchmark report.
[09:10] Luis: for benchmarking, can you run one test with logging enabled and one with logging off to see overhead?
[09:15] Jordan: yes — logging adds overhead; we'll run both and show delta.
[09:20] Samir: who on Redwood do I ping for VPC peering and KMS config?
[09:24] Maya: ping me (maya) for commercial and jordan for tech; we'll introduce engineering contact for peering.
[09:30] (short pause, background typing)
[09:34] Priya: ok — are there any gotchas we should watch for?
[09:36] Jordan: watch for token skews in your pre/post processing — those inflate cost. also watch sequence bucketing and batching; sometimes long tails break batch efficiency. recommend isolating long-form workflows to dedicated routes.
[09:52] Luis: could we run the long-form summarization on an asynchronous worker pool rather than the main low-latency path?
[09:58] Maya: yes that's a good design — route the 5% long tail to async workers with longer p95 budget; real-time route remains optimized for the 95%.
[10:07] Priya: last question — do you have a one-pager with the reserved+burst example we discussed?
[10:11] Maya: yes we'll send a one-pager along with cost scenarios and the benchmark template, plus security docs.
[10:16] Jordan: and we'll include a sample fallback policy + rollout IaC snippet for your infra team.
[10:22] Priya: great. if we get the traces by Thursday we'll be ready.
[10:26] Maya: perfect. recap of action items: maya send pricing and one-pager; jordan send benchmark template and IaC snippet; helio team send traces and KMS contact. schedule benchmark for week of 11/15.
[10:38] Priya: thanks, looking forward to it.
[10:41] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the attachments. bye.
